examples.solution_text:
The word **from** identifies where to stand. Measure clockwise from north at that point.
Bearing of $B$ from $A$: $072^\circ\text{T}$.
Bearing of $A$ from $B$: $252^\circ\text{T}$.

examples.question_text: The bearing of a shelter $S$ from a lake $L$ is $283^\circ\text{T}$. Find the bearing of $L$ from $S$.

examples.solution_text:
(a) Both angles are measured at $P$. Add the clockwise turn.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}48^\circ+70^\circ\\&=118^\circ\end{aligned}$
The bearing of $R$ from $P$ is $118^\circ\text{T}$.
(b) Subtract the anticlockwise turn. It passes through north, so add $360^\circ$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}48^\circ-80^\circ+360^\circ\\&=328^\circ\end{aligned}$
The bearing of $V$ from $P$ is $328^\circ\text{T}$.

coverage.summary: Authored five worked examples covering the distinct assessed methods, including both reverse-bearing calculation orders and clockwise/anticlockwise turns. Questions and solutions are separate editable fields; solution prose and mathematics inherit renderer blue. Diagrams use black ordinary ink and blue solution annotations. Continuation gutters are authored where needed. Existing examples were absent. All 28 assessment locators are mapped; practice and quiz mathematics are unchanged. Final-size diagram typography and layout remain for the later visual stage.

examples.derivation: Read clockwise from north at the point named after 'from': B from A is 072°T; A from B is 252°T. These opposite bearings differ by 180°. The diagram explicitly states that it is not to scale.
Parallel north lines give c = 180° − 68° = 112°. The clockwise bearing at B is b = 360° − 112° = 248°T. The solution arcs mark the 112° anticlockwise angle and 248° clockwise bearing consistently.
At L, c = 360° − 283° = 77°. Parallel north lines give the bearing at S as b = 180° − 77° = 103°T. The joining line and both annotated arcs agree with these directions.
Construct the parallel north line at B. At A, c = 360° − 209° = 151°. Co-interior angles give b = 180° − 151° = 29°, written 029°T. The added north line and solution arcs agree with these angles.

At P, the clockwise turn gives 48° + 70° = 118°T. The anticlockwise turn crosses north: 48° − 80° + 360° = 328°T. TikZ directions 42°, −28° and 122° correspond to bearings 048°, 118° and 328° respectively.
